messages:
Devin (eng-platform): heads up — noticed a cluster of traces with missing child spans for /session-start around 2026-03-15T08:21Z. looks correlated with otel-collector-us-east flapping.
Maya (eng-sre): can you paste a trace id? i want to check ingress logs and nginx timeouts.
Devin (eng-platform): trace id: 0f8b3a7c4d9e2a11. quick snippet from agent logs right when it happened:
```
2026-03-15T08:20:58Z agent[pid=22]: exporter=http://otel-collector-us-east:4318 status=503 retry=1
2026-03-15T08:21:01Z agent[pid=22]: sampler=adaptive decided=drop child_count=3
2026-03-15T08:21:02Z agent[pid=22]: exporter=http://otel-collector-us-east:4318 status=200 retry=0
```
Anita (eng-observability): that pattern screams exporter-level transient 5xx causing the local sampler to switch heuristics. our adaptive sampler falls back to aggressive drop when exporter error_ratio > 0.5 for 1m window (current).
Leo (eng-infra): checking collector metrics now — i see exporter_send_errors spike at 08:20:57 and collector's retry/backoff kicked in. looks like an upstream ingress LB had a short backend flapping event.
infra-bot: otel-collector-us-east deployment restart detected: deployment/otel-collector-us-east restarted by kube-controller at 2026-03-15T08:22:10Z
Sam (eng-platform): can we avoid sampler flipping so quickly? app UX loses child spans and makes debugging impossible. maybe keep a grace period or reduce sensitivity.
Anita (eng-observability): agree. options: 1) increase the error ratio window from 1m -> 3m so single flaps don't flip policy, 2) add a temporary local queue so even if exporter errors, spans get buffered, 3) add an explicit fallback policy that prefers preserving children for high-cardinality routes (/session-start).
Devin (eng-platform): i'm leaning 3 for hot routes. we can mark route hints in the agent: route.allow_keep_children = true. small config snippet:
```yaml
routes:
  - match: "/session-start"
    sampling: auto
    preserve_child_spans: true
```
Leo (eng-infra): i can push a collector-side change to increase exporter_queue_size and enable retry_on_failure for 30s while we tune sampler. quick patch ready.
Maya (eng-sre): action items: Leo pushes collector queue fix (low-risk), Anita adjusts sampler window, Devin adds route hint for preserve_child_spans for hot routes, Sam adds dashboard/alert. i'll coordinate a canary after changes.
Sam (eng-platform): proposed alert metrics:
- otel.collector.exporter_errors / otel.collector.exporter_requests > 0.1 for 5m
- agent.sampler.drop_count > 0 for critical routes
- route.telemetry.child_span_drop_ratio > 0.02
Anita (eng-observability): adding a dedicated small panel to the platform console: "Exporter health & sampler impact" with those three. i will also add a regression alert to post to #incidents if child_span_drop_ratio spikes.
Devin (eng-platform): rolled a collector tweak to v1.7.3-canary at 08:40 UTC (bumped queue, enabled retry). initial traces look better — no more immediate sampler flip in the canary nodes.
trace-bot: trace 0f8b3a7c4d9e2a11 updated: spans restored after collector canary rollout.
Maya (eng-sre): confirmed nginx LB had a backend recycle at 08:20:55 (kube drain), that matches spike. long-term we should make LB drain less aggressive for telemetry backends.
Leo (eng-infra): filed infra ticket #INF-248 to investigate LB drain timing; mentioned in ticket to test slow-drain for telemetry pools.
Sam (eng-platform): follow-up PRs: #4023 (route hint support in agent), #4024 (sampler window change to 3m default), #4025 (console panel + alerts). tagging owners.
Anita (eng-observability): quick note: until route hints are widespread, setting a slightly larger exporter buffer and a short soft-fallback policy prevents one-off flaps from causing child drops. implemented as default in canary.
Devin (eng-platform): thanks all. next steps: roll canary to 25% tomorrow, keep an eye on child_span_drop_ratio for /session-start and /auth. if we still see drops we'll consider stronger buffering or a persistent local store.
Maya (eng-sre): created a short blameless incident note in #postmortems and linked INF-248. no user-facing outage, but telemetry quality regression — good catch. :wave:
Leo (eng-infra): ack, will follow up on LB config.
Devin (eng-platform): closing thread for now, will reopen if anomalies reappear. :thumbsup:
